source.title: Mechanistic Unveiling of Transformer Circuits: Self-Influence as a Key to Model Reasoning
source.authors: Lin Zhang; Lijie Hu; Di Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study applies alternative automatic circuit-finding methods to a fine-tuned GPT-2 on IOI and evaluates the resulting circuits' faithfulness, rather than reproducing the original head-level interventions.
record.gate_note: The study reports IOI circuit faithfulness and circuit compositions. Its token self-influence scores and inferred reasoning narratives do not directly test the named head classes or their roles, so they are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses the IOI dataset and task as a testbed for its self-influence framework (SICAF). Circuit finding with EAP, EAP-IG and EAP-IG-KL is a preliminary step, and the study only compares those methods' faithfulness and layer distributions with each other. The model is a GPT-2 fine-tuned on IOI data, not the pretrained GPT-2 small of the original. The study never compares its circuits with the Wang et al. 26-head circuit, its head classes or their roles. So its results do not bear on whether the original circuit holds (V1), whether other methods recover it (V4), or how its evaluation behaves (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SICAF (circuit finding plus layer-wise token self-influence) reveals a hierarchical, human-like reasoning process in fine-tuned GPT-2 on IOI. They also report that EAP-IG and EAP-IG-KL find more faithful circuits than EAP, and that nodes concentrate in the first and last few layers across all methods.
record.recipe_differences: Uses EAP, EAP-IG, and EAP-IG-KL edge-based circuit finding on fine-tuned GPT-2, followed by self-influence analysis; it does not reproduce the original head-level ablation and patching procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Circuit faithfulness and layerwise node distributions vary with circuit-finding method: EAP emphasizes final layers, while EAP-IG and EAP-IG-KL are described as more balanced; normalized faithfulness differs as well.

fits_no_version.finding: In a GPT-2 fine-tuned on IOI, EAP-IG and EAP-IG-KL circuits reach normalized faithfulness above 0.8 at about 800 edges, while EAP peaks below 0.6. The methods' circuits also differ in how their nodes are spread across layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Edge-attribution circuit-finding methods differ in the faithfulness and layer distribution of the IOI circuits they find in a fine-tuned GPT-2.

record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The experiment is limited to a fine-tuned GPT-2 and one task. The faithfulness comparisons are reported graphically, without uncertainty estimates; the text gives only broad performance-recovery statements. The study does not validate the original head roles by ablation or patching.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Circuit composition lists in Table 1 and token self-influence values in Tables 2 and 5-7 were not separately recorded: the former do not test the original head roles, and the latter measure token influence rather than the claim's named circuit behaviour.

untested.parts: The 26-head, 7-class circuit, the head roles, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria in pretrained GPT-2 small are not examined.
Backup name-mover takeover after ablation is not tested.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints and component reuse are not tested. The fine-tuned GPT-2 is not compared with the original circuit.
No overlap or agreement between method-found circuits and the original circuit is measured.
Ablation type, metric and prompt distribution are not varied for the original circuit.
Name orders, templates and numbers of names are not compared.

missing.what: The circuit compositions include heads that match original IOI circuit heads (e.g. 0.1, 3.0, 5.5, 6.9, 7.3, 7.9, 8.6, 8.10, 9.6, 9.9, 10.0, 10.7), but the authors make no comparison. A future row could compute overlap with the original circuit if the study is reconsidered for V4.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's labels are withdrawn. The 'challenges V4' label confused differences between circuit-finding methods with failure to recover the original circuit, which was never compared. The V1 support and limits labels rested on faithfulness of different, method-found circuits in a fine-tuned model. The self-influence results are interpretive and do not measure the circuit's components or roles.

versions.untested_parts: It does not test the original 26-head, 7-class circuit, the stated roles of those head classes, or the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria as a whole; it evaluates faithfulness of newly identified circuits.
Backup-head takeover after ablating main name-mover heads is not tested.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints, and reuse of components for other tasks are not tested.
The study compares EAP, EAP-IG, and EAP-IG-KL, but does not compare ablation types or other faithfulness metrics.
It shows circuit faithfulness differs by circuit-finding method and is not complete, but does not vary ablation type, metric, or prompt distribution.
Different name orders, templates, and numbers of names are not compared as conditions.

relation.reason: The IOI circuit setting supplies a testbed for SICAF; the reported comparisons do not establish any listed claim version.

tranche.reason: SICAF uses circuit finding on IOI-fine-tuned GPT-2 and reports method faithfulness, node distributions and self-influence. It does not test recovery of the original circuit or its head roles.

source_check.notes: The paper reports both aggregate recovery of at least 85% and EAP normalized faithfulness below 0.6; retain these as separate source statements. Its in-text figure references are shifted: faithfulness is Figure 2 and node distributions are Figure 3.
